William Dean

Preserved Primary Document • dean-w.htm

William Dean was born in Kent Co., DE sometime around 1803. He was the son of Jesse Dean and his wife, Rebecca. According to Jesse's will, William and his brother, Jesse Dean Jr., were born before their father and mother married. Consequently it is unlikely that they were born on the Dean family farm along the main Dover to Smyrna Rd. On December 9, 1824 William Dean married Ann Cork in Duck Creek Hundred. {DE Marriage Bond: Vol 21, pg 344}. One (age 24-36) was living in Duck Creek Hundred with a wife and three children. The other (age 10-24) was living in Dover Hundred with a wife and one child. It is not clear yet which was our William but they were probably related. After he inherited part of his father's farm in 1839, William and his family moved to Little Creek Hundred to the five acres he inherited on the east side of the main Dover to Smyrna road. He was a farmer and he appears in the 1840 records enumerated next door to his brother, Jesse Dean (d.1868). Again the census shows two William Deans living in Kent County DE and, again, it is difficult to determine which is the son of Jesse and Rebecca but the fact that brother Jesse Jr. was enumerated on page 35 suggests the William on page 34 was his brother and both were living on the land they inherited from their father.
